title: The Tally Mark Surprise
markdown:
The Science Club at Oak Tree Elementary had a big decision: who would be their new club pet? They had three fluffy, sleek, or chirpy friends to pick from: Cottonpuff the bunny, Slinky the snake, and Pip the parrot.

Iris, who loved puzzles, tapped her chin. “We need to know what everyone wants, to be fair.”

Button the badger nodded. “Yes! But how do we count all these paper slips with names?” The slips fluttered like confetti. It was a paper snowstorm, names sliding under chairs and hiding in Button’s fur.

Iris sighed. “Oh dear. It’s like trying to count a million leaves.”

Professor Elm chuckled, kind as a coat on a peg. “How do we untangle big messes? With a clever system.”

Iris’s eyes lit up. “A system for counting!” She grabbed a shiny blue pencil. “What if we make a mark for every vote?” She drew a straight line on paper. Then another. Then another. “Now,” she said, drawing a line right across them, “this is a group of five. It’s called a tally. It makes counting super fast. A shortcut for your brain.”

Professor Elm smiled. “Exactly, Iris. Tally marks help organise information. Like sorting bricks by colour.”

So they started. Button smoothed a slip. “Cottonpuff!” Iris’s pencil scritched a tally mark for Cottonpuff. “Slinky!” Iris added a mark for Slinky. Then, “Pip!” another for Pip. Their pencils danced. Every time they reached five marks, Iris drew that neat little fence. The paper filled with neat little groups, and the snowstorm of slips became a quiet pile of counted ones.

Soon the chart was full. Cottonpuff had six groups of five. That’s thirty votes. Slinky had three groups of five. That’s fifteen votes. And Pip had eight groups of five. A whopping forty votes for Pip.

Button clapped his paws. “Hooray for Pip!”

Professor Elm beamed. “You see? Tally marks helped us organise all that information. Scientists use tally charts for experiments. It helps them gather facts, like clues for a detective.”

Iris nodded, that happy puzzle-click feeling bubbling inside her. “So tally marks help us count big numbers fast and see which one is the biggest?”

“Precisely. It helps us make smart decisions. And now Pip will be joining our Science Club. Welcome, Pip.”

Pip chirped happily, as if the fence-marks on the paper had been a nest all along. Button did a happy dance. Iris smiled, thinking about all the amazing things they could count. She watched ants march in a line across the windowsill. “I wonder if tally marks could help us count them?”

Professor Elm laughed. “An excellent question. The world is full of things to count.” Pip chirped again, as if to say more learning, please—especially if the next flock came in fives.
characters: Iris (puzzle solver), Button (nodding badger), Elm (chuckling professor)
